## Original request (top authority)

# Tabula: seven more commands

This repository already holds **tabula**, a small Python tool I use on CSV files (Python 3.9 or newer, standard
library only). Read the code first: `README.md`, `tabula/engine.py` and `tests/`. It has four commands today (`show`,
`head`, `cols`, `apply`), reads CSV files, and prints a table as text, CSV or JSON. I want seven more commands. They
all go into the same module, `tabula/engine.py`, the way the first four did: a `cmd_NAME(args, opts)` function that
returns a `Table`, one entry in `COMMANDS`. Keep what is there working: the four commands, their output, their exit
statuses, and `pip install .` giving the `tabula` command and `import tabula`. Each command also gets its own test file `tests/test_COMMAND.py`, a section in `docs/commands.md` (one section per
command, in the order of the sections below, written like the four that are there) and a line in the command list of `README.md`.

How a command behaves in general is already settled by the code and stays as it is: `--format text|csv|json` (text by
default) says how the result table is printed; a mistake in a file or in what I asked for prints
`tabula: <message>` on standard error and exits 1, with nothing on standard output; a command line that is not shaped
right (a missing argument, an unknown option, a condition with no operator) exits 2. A "row N" in a message counts the
data rows of the file from 1, the header not counted, in the order of the file (not the sorted order). Cell values are
text; a **number** is what `to_decimal` accepts (an optional sign, digits, an optional decimal point; no exponent, no
thousands marks). All arithmetic is exact (`Decimal`), never floating point. A column named in a request that the file
does not have is a mistake in the request (exit 1, the message names the column).

Two options are new and are read by one command each, but they are accepted on any command line, before or after the
command: `--kind inner|left` and `--keep first|last`, each as `--opt value` or `--opt=value`. Any other value is a
usage error (exit 2).

The original request outranks the PRD, which outranks the issue. Where they conflict, follow the original request and say so in the PR.

OUTPUT STYLE — caveman, rules inlined here. For your own output and agent-to-agent comments:
handoffs, review findings, checkpoint notes — no human reads them live. Terse: drop articles, filler, pleasantries;
fragments are fine; short synonyms; arrows for causality (X -> Y); technical terms stay exact.
Human-facing artifacts stay plain prose, never caveman: PRD and issue bodies, PR titles and descriptions,
docs, README, CHANGELOG, commit messages. Exact strings are never compressed: code, commands, errors,
file paths, test names, label names, issue and PR refs, `<!-- harness-… -->` marker lines, the promise.

SHARED HOST — stop a background job only by the PID you started (`$!`, or a PID file you wrote) —
never `pkill -f`, `killall`, or `ps … | grep … | kill` by pattern. This host runs many lanes; a
pattern kill can hit theirs.
A PID read from a file or variable must be checked as non-empty, all digits and greater than 1
before it reaches `kill` or `pgrep -P`. Never write `pgrep -P ${p:-0}`: a missing or empty pidfile
becomes PID 0, `pgrep -P 0` lists PID 1's children, and killing them takes down `systemd --user` and
every fleet on the host. Never signal PID 0, PID 1 or a negative PID.
LONG WAITS (#1042, #1066) — never wait inside your session; the engine waits for you. Your prompt cache lives 5 minutes: a foreground `sleep` loop that wakes after 9-10 minutes rewrites your whole context as a cache write (150K-300K tokens, about $1 per wake on Sonnet, against about $0.08 for a cache read), and that pattern was 72% of three days' spend. A job that may run longer than about 4 minutes (a suite, a gate, a bench batch, a Windows-host run, a build): start it with `harness-wait run --deadline-s <most seconds it may take> --log <logfile> -- <command…>`, then END YOUR TURN at once: one short reply naming what you wait for (no promise, no more tool calls). `harness-wait run` starts the command detached, keeps its output in the log and its exit code in `<logfile>.rc`, and writes your wait spec; the engine checks it for you at no model cost and resumes this session ONCE, when the job exits or the deadline passes, with `wait done: <condition>, rc=<n>, log tail: …`. Judge the result from that message and read the log for more; never loop on it. Other conditions: `harness-wait set --deadline-s <s> --pid <pid>` (a process exits), `--path <file>` (a file appears), `--regex <re> --log <file>` (a line appears in a log from now on). Not allowed, whatever the Bash timeout: `for i in $(seq 1 58); do …; sleep 10; done`, `timeout 585 bash -c "until …"`, `end=$((SECONDS+570)); while …`, or a Bash `run_in_background` you then keep polling. A wait on another lane (a lock queue, a merge, a PR) is not a job you can run: park the lane where a park exists (a lock queue, #1034) instead of polling. A usage limit needs nothing from you: the engine parks the lane and resumes it once the limit has cleared. If you park yourself on a limit or a reset time (`harness-wait set --limit --until <epoch>`), omit `--deadline-s`: the deadline resumes you too, and `waitlib` refuses one that ends before `--until` (#1100). A wait that ends HOURS from now (more than 2 hours: a bench or budget block waiting for a usage window to reset, `harness-wait set --limit --until <epoch>`, or `--path <file> --deadline-s <s>`) PARKS you (#1154): commit and push first, then run it; it posts your handoff, swaps `agent-working` for the `waiting-quota` label and ends your session, so your pool slot goes to the next ready issue, and the engine re-dispatches the issue as a resume once the wait is over — do nothing more after it prints `PARKED`. A refusal (unpushed work) leaves your session as it was; `--resume inject` keeps your slot, and is for waits you really must hold. Never sit on a pool slot for hours. Polling you cannot avoid: one short check per wake, each wake under 270 seconds so the cache stays warm. Never a blocking loop. SUB-AGENTS (#1249) — your own sub-agents are not jobs you can wait on, and each one's notification is a wake after the 5-minute cache expired (140K-350K tokens of cache write each; four bangwa lanes were parked for it). Sub-agents always run in the background here. Start every sub-agent of one fan-out in ONE message, so they start together and tend to finish together. Every sub-agent brief tells it to run every command in the foreground: no `run_in_background`, `Monitor` or `harness-wait run` inside a sub-agent, and never end its turn before its final report. Each sub-agent then notifies you exactly once; one that backgrounds its work and ends its turn sends an interim "completed" you pay a wake for, and a second when it really finishes. When a sub-agent's notification arrives while other sub-agents are still running, make no tool calls: write one short line and end your turn (no re-reading files, no `git status`, no check on the others). Never poll a sub-agent (`TaskOutput`, reading its output file, or `sleep`). SUB-AGENT SCOPE (#1252) — every call re-reads your whole context from cache: on one fleet that was 65% of its spend, with lanes at 695k and sub-agents at 804k tokens and no compaction ever. The engine sets a context budget (`HARNESS_LANE_CONTEXT_MAX`, default 200k) and Claude Code compacts a lane and each of its sub-agents when it reaches it; stay well under it yourself. A sub-agent is ONE bounded task: its brief names the files it reads and edits, the tests it runs and the checkboxes it owns, and nothing more. # Tabula: seven more commands

This repository already holds **tabula**, a small Python tool I use on CSV files (Python 3.9 or newer, standard
library only). Read the code first: `README.md`, `tabula/engine.py` and `tests/`. It has four commands today (`show`,
`head`, `cols`, `apply`), reads CSV files, and prints a table as text, CSV or JSON. I want seven more commands. They
all go into the same module, `tabula/engine.py`, the way the first four did: a `cmd_NAME(args, opts)` function that
returns a `Table`, one entry in `COMMANDS`. Keep what is there working: the four commands, their output, their exit
statuses, and `pip install .` giving the `tabula` command and `import tabula`. Each command also gets its own test file `tests/test_COMMAND.py`, a section in `docs/commands.md` (one section per
command, in the order of the sections below, written like the four that are there) and a line in the command list of `README.md`.

How a command behaves in general is already settled by the code and stays as it is: `--format text|csv|json` (text by
default) says how the result table is printed; a mistake in a file or in what I asked for prints
`tabula: <message>` on standard error and exits 1, with nothing on standard output; a command line that is not shaped
right (a missing argument, an unknown option, a condition with no operator) exits 2. A "row N" in a message counts the
data rows of the file from 1, the header not counted, in the order of the file (not the sorted order). Cell values are
text; a **number** is what `to_decimal` accepts (an optional sign, digits, an optional decimal point; no exponent, no
thousands marks). All arithmetic is exact (`Decimal`), never floating point. A column named in a request that the file
does not have is a mistake in the request (exit 1, the message names the column).

Two options are new and are read by one command each, but they are accepted on any command line, before or after the
command: `--kind inner|left` and `--keep first|last`, each as `--opt value` or `--opt=value`. Any other value is a
usage error (exit 2).

## sort

`tabula sort FILE KEY...` prints the rows sorted by the first KEY, ties by the second, and so on. A KEY is a column
name, optionally followed by the modifiers `:num` (compare as numbers, not as text) and `:desc` (largest first), in
either order (`price:num:desc`, `price:desc:num`). Text compares by code point (so `B` sorts before `a`). The sort is
stable: rows that tie on every key keep the order of the file, also with `:desc`. With `:num`, a cell that is not a
number is a mistake: `FILE: row N: column 'price': 'abc' is not a number`. A modifier given twice in one KEY is a usage
error. At least one KEY is needed.

## filter

`tabula filter FILE CONDITION...` prints the rows where every CONDITION holds, in the order of the file. A CONDITION
is one argument shaped `COLUMN OP VALUE` with no spaces added: `price>=10`, `city==Leeds`, `name~gnome`. The operators
are `==`, `!=`, `>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<` and `~` (the cell contains VALUE, ignoring upper and lower case). The operator is
the first one that appears in the argument (so a column name cannot contain one of them), and where two start at the
same place the longer one (`>=` and not `>`). For every operator but `~`, when both the cell and VALUE are numbers
they are compared as numbers (`10` is greater than `9`, `1.0` equals `1`); otherwise as text, by code point. An
argument with no operator, or nothing before the operator, is a usage error. At least one CONDITION is needed. A
table with no row left still prints its header.

## group

`tabula group FILE BY AGGREGATE...` prints one row per distinct value of column BY, in the order each value first
appears, with the columns BY and then one per AGGREGATE, named as written with `:` replaced by `_` (`sum_qty`). An
AGGREGATE is `count` (rows in the group) or `sum:COLUMN`, `min:COLUMN`, `max:COLUMN`, `mean:COLUMN` over the numbers of
that column. `sum`, `min` and `max` are printed as plain numbers (no `+` sign, no exponent; `10.50` stays `10.50`).
`mean` is the exact sum divided by the count, rounded half up to two decimals and always printed with two (`5.00`,
`2.25`). A cell that is not a number in a column being summed, compared or averaged is a mistake (the same
message as in `sort`). At least one AGGREGATE is needed; one that is not one of those, or the same one twice, is a
usage error.

## join

`tabula join LEFT RIGHT KEY` joins two files on the column KEY, which both must have. The result has the columns of
LEFT, then the columns of RIGHT except KEY. A RIGHT column whose name LEFT already has gets `_right` added to its name.
If that still leaves two columns of the same name the result cannot be printed: that is a mistake. Values match when
the text is exactly equal. With `--kind inner` (the default) the rows are, for each LEFT row in the order of LEFT, one
row per matching RIGHT row in the order of RIGHT; a LEFT row with no match is left out. With `--kind left` a LEFT row
with no match appears once, with empty text in the RIGHT columns. Exactly three arguments are needed.

## pivot

`tabula pivot FILE ROW COLUMN VALUE` turns the distinct values of column COLUMN into columns. The result has the column
ROW, then one column per distinct value of COLUMN in the order each first appears; one row per distinct value of ROW in
the order each first appears. A cell is the exact sum of the numbers in VALUE for the rows with that ROW and that
COLUMN value, printed as in `group`; a pair that never occurs is `0`. ROW and COLUMN must be different columns (usage
error otherwise). An empty value in COLUMN is a mistake (`FILE: row N: column 'C': empty value`), and so is a value of
COLUMN equal to the name of the ROW column, because the result would have a column name twice. A non-number in VALUE is
a mistake as in `sort`. Exactly four arguments are needed.

## dedupe

`tabula dedupe FILE KEY...` drops rows whose values in all the KEY columns equal those of another row (text equality).
With `--keep first` (the default) the first row of each such set stays; with `--keep last` the last one stays. The
rows that stay keep the relative order they have in the file. At least one KEY is needed.

## stats

`tabula stats FILE COLUMN...` prints one row per COLUMN, in the order asked, with the columns `column`, `count`, `min`,
`max`, `mean`, `median`. The statistics are over the cells of that column that are not empty (a cell of only
whitespace counts as empty); all of those must be numbers (mistake as in `sort` otherwise). `count` is how many there
are. `min` and `max` print as in `group`; `mean` and `median` are rounded half up to two decimals and always printed
with two (the median of an even count is the mean of the two middle numbers, taken exactly). With no numbers at all the
row is `COLUMN`, `0` and four empty cells. At least one COLUMN is needed.

File this as seven issues, one per command, so each can be built, tested and merged on its own. The seven commands do
not depend on each other, but they share the module, the option reading, the number helpers, `docs/commands.md` and the
README list, so expect to touch the same lines as the others. Finish the module's own conventions before adding to them:
do not add a second way to do something it already does.

## Problem Statement

`tabula` (a standard-library-only Python 3.9+ CLI over CSV files, everything in `tabula/engine.py`) has four commands: `show`, `head`, `cols`, `apply`. The user needs seven more table operations — `sort`, `filter`, `group`, `join`, `pivot`, `dedupe`, `stats` — with exact `Decimal` arithmetic, the same error/exit conventions, and the same output formats (`--format text|csv|json`).

## Solution

Add seven commands to `tabula/engine.py`, each a `cmd_NAME(args, opts)` returning a `Table` and one entry in `COMMANDS`, plus two new global options (`--kind inner|left`, `--keep first|last`). Each command gets `tests/test_NAME.py`, a section in `docs/commands.md` (after `apply`, in the order sort, filter, group, join, pivot, dedupe, stats, written like the existing four) and a line in the README command list. Everything existing keeps working unchanged: the four commands, their output and exit statuses, `pip install .` giving the `tabula` script and `import tabula`.

**Decomposition: exactly seven issues, one per command** (sort, filter, group, join, pivot, dedupe, stats), none blocked by another. Each must be buildable, testable and mergeable on its own. The shared groundwork (below) is NOT a separate issue: each issue adds whatever piece of it it needs if that piece is not on `main` yet, exactly as specified here (same name, same signature), and reuses it if it is. Expect to rebase over the same lines (`COMMANDS`, `parse_args`, the README list, `docs/commands.md`).

## User Stories

1. As a CSV user, I want `tabula sort FILE KEY...` with `:num`/`:desc` modifiers, so that I can order rows by several keys, stably.
2. As a CSV user, I want `tabula filter FILE CONDITION...` (`== != >= <= > < ~`), so that I keep only rows meeting every condition, comparing numbers as numbers.
3. As a CSV user, I want `tabula group FILE BY AGGREGATE...` (`count`, `sum/min/max/mean:COL`), so that I can summarise per group exactly.
4. As a CSV user, I want `tabula join LEFT RIGHT KEY` with `--kind inner|left`, so that I can combine two files.
5. As a CSV user, I want `tabula pivot FILE ROW COLUMN VALUE`, so that distinct values become columns holding exact sums.
6. As a CSV user, I want `tabula dedupe FILE KEY...` with `--keep first|last`, so that duplicate rows go away while order is kept.
7. As a CSV user, I want `tabula stats FILE COLUMN...` (count, min, max, mean, median), so that I can describe numeric columns.
8. As a user, I want every mistake to print `tabula: <message>` on stderr with exit 1 and nothing on stdout, and a badly shaped command line to exit 2, as today.

## Implementation Decisions

### Shared groundwork — finish the module's conventions, never add a second way
- **Options**: `parse_args` today handles `--format` with inline code. Generalise it to ONE table-driven path, e.g. `OPTIONS = {"format": ("text", "csv", "json"), "kind": ("inner", "left"), "keep": ("first", "last")}` with defaults `{"format": "text", "kind": "inner", "keep": "first"}`; every option accepts `--opt value` and `--opt=value`, anywhere on the line (before or after the command); a missing value or a value not in the list is a `UsageError` (same message shape as `--format` today: `--kind must be one of inner, left, got 'x'`; `--kind needs a value`). The last occurrence wins. All three are accepted on every command line; a command that does not read one ignores it. `FORMATS` stays (it is used elsewhere / may be imported). `--format` behaviour and messages must not change.
- **Argument counts**: `_need_args(args, count, usage)` exists for exact counts; `cmd_apply` checks "at least" inline. Extend the one helper rather than adding another: e.g. `_need_args(args, count, usage, at_least=False)` and use it in `cmd_apply` too (message unchanged: `usage: tabula apply FILE COLUMN TRANSFORM...`).
- **Row mistakes**: `cmd_apply` builds `"%s: row %d: %s"` inline. Add one helper `_row_error(table, number, message)` (returns/raises the `TabulaError` `FILE: row N: message`) and use it in `cmd_apply` and every new command. Row numbers are data rows from 1, header not counted, in FILE order (never sorted order).
- **Numbers in cells**: one helper `_cell_number(table, number, column, value)` built on the existing `_need_number`/`to_decimal`, raising `FILE: row N: column 'price': 'abc' is not a number`. Used by sort `:num`, group, pivot, stats. Do not add another number parser; `to_decimal` defines a number (it strips surrounding whitespace).
- **Printing numbers**: sums/min/max print with the existing `fmt_decimal` (no `+`, no exponent, trailing zeros kept: `10.50` stays `10.50`, `-0` prints `0`). Add one helper `fmt_2dp(number)` = `fmt_decimal(number.quantize(Decimal("0.01"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))` for mean/median (always two decimals: `5.00`, `2.25`). Reuse the rounding approach `t_round_to` already uses.
- **Column lookup**: `Table.index(name)` already raises `FILE: no column 'x' (columns: ...)` — use it for every column named in a request (exit 1, message names the column). Never re-implement it.
- **Case-insensitive contains**: `t_icontains` already defines "contains, case aside" (`arg.lower() in value.lower()`); filter `~` must use the same rule (call it or share its logic), not a different one such as `casefold`.
- Text comparisons are by code point (plain Python `str` ordering). Equality for join/dedupe/group keys/pivot keys is exact text equality (no stripping).
- Each command's `COMMANDS` entry has a usage string like the existing ones (`"sort FILE KEY..."`, `"filter FILE CONDITION..."`, `"group FILE BY AGGREGATE..."`, `"join LEFT RIGHT KEY"`, `"pivot FILE ROW COLUMN VALUE"`, `"dedupe FILE KEY..."`, `"stats FILE COLUMN..."`) and a short description. Usage errors print `usage: tabula <usage>` like `_need_args` does.
- Usage errors are detected from the arguments before or regardless of the file (a malformed KEY/CONDITION/AGGREGATE is exit 2 even if FILE does not exist). Then file/column mistakes are exit 1.

### Per-command decisions (ambiguities resolved)
- **sort**: KEY = `NAME[:mod[:mod]]`, mods ∈ {`num`, `desc`}, any order. An unknown modifier, a modifier repeated, or an empty column name is a usage error (exit 2). Multi-key stable sort (e.g. sort by keys from last to first with Python's stable `sorted`; `reverse=True` keeps ties in file order). `:num` on a non-number cell (including empty) → `FILE: row N: column 'C': 'abc' is not a number` (N = file row).
- **filter**: operator = earliest position in the argument; at equal position the longer wins (`>=` over `>`, `==`/`!=` are two chars; a lone `=` or `!` is not an operator). No operator, or empty column part → usage error. VALUE may be empty (`name==` matches empty cells; `name~` matches every row). Numeric comparison when both cell and VALUE satisfy `to_decimal`; else code-point text comparison (`==`/`!=` then compare raw text exactly). Header always printed, even with no rows left.
- **group**: output columns = BY, then each aggregate named with `:` → `_` (`count`, `sum_qty`, `mean_price`). Aggregates: `count`, `sum:C`, `min:C`, `max:C`, `mean:C`; anything else (unknown name, `count:x`, `sum` without column, empty column) or the same aggregate twice → usage error. Unknown column in an aggregate → exit 1. Every cell of an aggregated column (except for `count`) must be a number, else the sort-style row message. If an output column name equals BY (e.g. BY is named `count` and `count` is asked), the result would have a duplicate column → mistake, exit 1 (`group: column 'count' would appear twice`). mean = exact sum / count, `fmt_2dp`. min/max print the original number via `fmt_decimal(Decimal)`.
- **join**: exactly 3 args else usage error. KEY must exist in both files (exit 1 naming the column and file, via `Table.index`). Result columns: LEFT's, then RIGHT's except KEY, with `_right` appended to any RIGHT name LEFT already has; if a name is still duplicated → exit 1 (message names the column). Inner: per LEFT row in order, one row per matching RIGHT row in RIGHT order. Left: unmatched LEFT row once, RIGHT columns empty text. `--kind` comes from the shared option table.
- **pivot**: exactly 4 args else usage error; ROW == COLUMN → usage error. VALUE may equal ROW or COLUMN (it is just summed). Empty COLUMN value → `FILE: row N: column 'C': empty value` (empty = empty or only whitespace, matching how headers treat blank names). A COLUMN value equal to the ROW column name → exit 1 `FILE: row N: column 'C': value 'X' is the name of the row column`. Non-number VALUE → sort-style message. Missing pair → `0`. Sums via `fmt_decimal`. Checks are made in file order, the first offending row is reported.
- **dedupe**: ≥1 KEY else usage error; `--keep first` (default) / `last`; survivors keep file order.
- **stats**: ≥1 COLUMN; one output row per COLUMN in the order asked (a repeated column gives a repeated row). Columns `column,count,min,max,mean,median`. Empty or whitespace-only cells skipped; the rest must be numbers (sort-style message). No numbers → `COLUMN,0,,,,`. Median of even count = exact mean of the two middle values, then `fmt_2dp`.

### Constraints
- Standard library only, must run on Python 3.9 (no `match` statements, no `X | Y` type syntax or other 3.10+ features).
- Arithmetic only with `Decimal` (context precision 60 already set); never `float`.

## Testing Decisions

- Each command: `tests/test_NAME.py`, `unittest`, runnable with `python -m unittest discover tests`. Test through the CLI (subprocess `python -m tabula`, like `CliTests.run_cli` in `tests/test_engine.py`) for stdout, exit status and stderr emptiness/non-emptiness, and exact stderr message text for the specified messages; plus direct `engine.cmd_NAME` / `engine.main` calls where helpful.
- Cover: each format (text/csv/json) at least once per command; every usage-error case (exit 2, empty stdout); every mistake case (exit 1, empty stdout, exact message); the new options in both `--opt value` and `--opt=value` forms and before/after the command; invalid option values (exit 2).
- `tests/test_engine.py` must keep passing unchanged (existing behaviour is frozen). Add a regression check that `--kind`/`--keep` are accepted on `show`.
- `pip install .` in a temporary venv must still give a working `tabula` command and `import tabula` (verify at least once, e.g. in review).

## Out of Scope

- New transforms, changes to `show/head/cols/apply` behaviour or output, new output formats.
- Third-party dependencies, packaging changes beyond what is needed (version bump optional).
- Options other than `--format`, `--kind`, `--keep`.

- [ ] Seven `cmd_*` functions (`sort`, `filter`, `group`, `join`, `pivot`, `dedupe`, `stats`) in `tabula/engine.py`, each one entry in `COMMANDS`, returning a `Table`.
- [ ] `--kind inner|left` and `--keep first|last` accepted on any command line, before or after the command, as `--opt value` or `--opt=value`; any other value or a missing value exits 2; parsed by the same table-driven path as `--format`.

- [ ] All arithmetic is `Decimal`; no `float` anywhere in the new code.
- [ ] Shared helpers used, not duplicated: one option table, one `_need_args`, one row-error helper, one cell-number helper, `fmt_decimal` + one 2-dp formatter; `cmd_apply` uses the shared helpers with unchanged messages.

## Problem Statement

`tabula` (a standard-library-only Python 3.9+ CLI over CSV files, everything in `tabula/engine.py`) has four commands: `show`, `head`, `cols`, `apply`. The user needs seven more table operations — `sort`, `filter`, `group`, `join`, `pivot`, `dedupe`, `stats` — with exact `Decimal` arithmetic, the same error/exit conventions, and the same output formats (`--format text|csv|json`).

## Solution

Add seven commands to `tabula/engine.py`, each a `cmd_NAME(args, opts)` returning a `Table` and one entry in `COMMANDS`, plus two new global options (`--kind inner|left`, `--keep first|last`). Each command gets `tests/test_NAME.py`, a section in `docs/commands.md` (after `apply`, in the order sort, filter, group, join, pivot, dedupe, stats, written like the existing four) and a line in the README command list. Everything existing keeps working unchanged: the four commands, their output and exit statuses, `pip install .` giving the `tabula` script and `import tabula`.

**Decomposition: exactly seven issues, one per command** (sort, filter, group, join, pivot, dedupe, stats), none blocked by another. Each must be buildable, testable and mergeable on its own. The shared groundwork (below) is NOT a separate issue: each issue adds whatever piece of it it needs if that piece is not on `main` yet, exactly as specified here (same name, same signature), and reuses it if it is. Expect to rebase over the same lines (`COMMANDS`, `parse_args`, the README list, `docs/commands.md`).

## User Stories

1. As a CSV user, I want `tabula sort FILE KEY...` with `:num`/`:desc` modifiers, so that I can order rows by several keys, stably.
2. As a CSV user, I want `tabula filter FILE CONDITION...` (`== != >= <= > < ~`), so that I keep only rows meeting every condition, comparing numbers as numbers.
3. As a CSV user, I want `tabula group FILE BY AGGREGATE...` (`count`, `sum/min/max/mean:COL`), so that I can summarise per group exactly.
4. As a CSV user, I want `tabula join LEFT RIGHT KEY` with `--kind inner|left`, so that I can combine two files.
5. As a CSV user, I want `tabula pivot FILE ROW COLUMN VALUE`, so that distinct values become columns holding exact sums.
6. As a CSV user, I want `tabula dedupe FILE KEY...` with `--keep first|last`, so that duplicate rows go away while order is kept.
7. As a CSV user, I want `tabula stats FILE COLUMN...` (count, min, max, mean, median), so that I can describe numeric columns.
8. As a user, I want every mistake to print `tabula: <message>` on stderr with exit 1 and nothing on stdout, and a badly shaped command line to exit 2, as today.

## Implementation Decisions

### Shared groundwork — finish the module's conventions, never add a second way
- **Options**: `parse_args` today handles `--format` with inline code. Generalise it to ONE table-driven path, e.g. `OPTIONS = {"format": ("text", "csv", "json"), "kind": ("inner", "left"), "keep": ("first", "last")}` with defaults `{"format": "text", "kind": "inner", "keep": "first"}`; every option accepts `--opt value` and `--opt=value`, anywhere on the line (before or after the command); a missing value or a value not in the list is a `UsageError` (same message shape as `--format` today: `--kind must be one of inner, left, got 'x'`; `--kind needs a value`). The last occurrence wins. All three are accepted on every command line; a command that does not read one ignores it. `FORMATS` stays (it is used elsewhere / may be imported). `--format` behaviour and messages must not change.
- **Argument counts**: `_need_args(args, count, usage)` exists for exact counts; `cmd_apply` checks "at least" inline. Extend the one helper rather than adding another: e.g. `_need_args(args, count, usage, at_least=False)` and use it in `cmd_apply` too (message unchanged: `usage: tabula apply FILE COLUMN TRANSFORM...`).
- **Row mistakes**: `cmd_apply` builds `"%s: row %d: %s"` inline. Add one helper `_row_error(table, number, message)` (returns/raises the `TabulaError` `FILE: row N: message`) and use it in `cmd_apply` and every new command. Row numbers are data rows from 1, header not counted, in FILE order (never sorted order).
- **Numbers in cells**: one helper `_cell_number(table, number, column, value)` built on the existing `_need_number`/`to_decimal`, raising `FILE: row N: column 'price': 'abc' is not a number`. - **Printing numbers**: sums/min/max print with the existing `fmt_decimal` (no `+`, no exponent, trailing zeros kept: `10.50` stays `10.50`, `-0` prints `0`). - **Column lookup**: `Table.index(name)` already raises `FILE: no column 'x' (columns: ...)` — use it for every column named in a request (exit 1, message names the column). Never re-implement it.
- **Case-insensitive contains**: `t_icontains` already defines "contains, case aside" (`arg.lower() in value.lower()`); filter `~` must use the same rule (call it or share its logic), not a different one such as `casefold`.
- Text comparisons are by code point (plain Python `str` ordering). Equality for join/dedupe/group keys/pivot keys is exact text equality (no stripping).

### Per-command decisions (ambiguities resolved)
- **sort**: KEY = `NAME[:mod[:mod]]`, mods ∈ {`num`, `desc`}, any order. An unknown modifier, a modifier repeated, or an empty column name is a usage error (exit 2). Multi-key stable sort (e.g. sort by keys from last to first with Python's stable `sorted`; `reverse=True` keeps ties in file order). `:num` on a non-number cell (including empty) → `FILE: row N: column 'C': 'abc' is not a number` (N = file row).
- **filter**: operator = earliest position in the argument; at equal position the longer wins (`>=` over `>`, `==`/`!=` are two chars; a lone `=` or `!` is not an operator). No operator, or empty column part → usage error. VALUE may be empty (`name==` matches empty cells; `name~` matches every row). Numeric comparison when both cell and VALUE satisfy `to_decimal`; else code-point text comparison (`==`/`!=` then compare raw text exactly). Header always printed, even with no rows left.
- **group**: output columns = BY, then each aggregate named with `:` → `_` (`count`, `sum_qty`, `mean_price`). Aggregates: `count`, `sum:C`, `min:C`, `max:C`, `mean:C`; anything else (unknown name, `count:x`, `sum` without column, empty column) or the same aggregate twice → usage error. Unknown column in an aggregate → exit 1. Every cell of an aggregated column (except for `count`) must be a number, else the sort-style row message. If an output column name equals BY (e.g. BY is named `count` and `count` is asked), the result would have a duplicate column → mistake, exit 1 (`group: column 'count' would appear twice`). mean = exact sum / count, `fmt_2dp`. min/max print the original number via `fmt_decimal(Decimal)`.
- **join**: exactly 3 args else usage error. KEY must exist in both files (exit 1 naming the column and file, via `Table.index`). Result columns: LEFT's, then RIGHT's except KEY, with `_right` appended to any RIGHT name LEFT already has; if a name is still duplicated → exit 1 (message names the column). Inner: per LEFT row in order, one row per matching RIGHT row in RIGHT order. Left: unmatched LEFT row once, RIGHT columns empty text. `--kind` comes from the shared option table.
- **pivot**: exactly 4 args else usage error; ROW == COLUMN → usage error. VALUE may equal ROW or COLUMN (it is just summed). Empty COLUMN value → `FILE: row N: column 'C': empty value` (empty = empty or only whitespace, matching how headers treat blank names). A COLUMN value equal to the ROW column name → exit 1 `FILE: row N: column 'C': value 'X' is the name of the row column`. Non-number VALUE → sort-style message. Missing pair → `0`. Sums via `fmt_decimal`. Checks are made in file order, the first offending row is reported.
- **dedupe**: ≥1 KEY else usage error; `--keep first` (default) / `last`; survivors keep file order.
- **stats**: ≥1 COLUMN; one output row per COLUMN in the order asked (a repeated column gives a repeated row). Columns `column,count,min,max,mean,median`. Empty or whitespace-only cells skipped; the rest must be numbers (sort-style message). No numbers → `COLUMN,0,,,,`. Median of even count = exact mean of the two middle values, then `fmt_2dp`.

### Constraints
- Standard library only, must run on Python 3.9 (no `match` statements, no `X | Y` type syntax or other 3.10+ features).
- Arithmetic only with `Decimal` (context precision 60 already set); never `float`.

- Each command: `tests/test_NAME.py`, `unittest`, runnable with `python -m unittest discover tests`. Test through the CLI (subprocess `python -m tabula`, like `CliTests.run_cli` in `tests/test_engine.py`) for stdout, exit status and stderr emptiness/non-emptiness, and exact stderr message text for the specified messages; plus direct `engine.cmd_NAME` / `engine.main` calls where helpful.

If that still leaves two columns of the same name the result cannot be printed: that is a mistake. Values match when
the text is exactly equal. With `--kind inner` (the default) the rows are, for each LEFT row in the order of LEFT, one
row per matching RIGHT row in the order of RIGHT; a LEFT row with no match is left out. With `--kind left` a LEFT row
with no match appears once, with empty text in the RIGHT columns. Exactly three arguments are needed.

## pivot

`tabula pivot FILE ROW COLUMN VALUE` turns the distinct values of column COLUMN into columns. The result has the column
ROW, then one column per distinct value of COLUMN in the order each first appears; one row per distinct value of ROW in
the order each first appears. A cell is the exact sum of the numbers in VALUE for the rows with that ROW and that
COLUMN value, printed as in `group`; a pair that never occurs is `0`. ROW and COLUMN must be different columns (usage
error otherwise). An empty value in COLUMN is a mistake (`FILE: row N: column 'C': empty value`), and so is a value of
COLUMN equal to the name of the ROW column, because the result would have a column name twice. A non-number in VALUE is
a mistake as in `sort`. Exactly four arguments are needed.

## dedupe

`tabula dedupe FILE KEY...` drops rows whose values in all the KEY columns equal those of another row (text equality).
With `--keep first` (the default) the first row of each such set stays; with `--keep last` the last one stays. The
rows that stay keep the relative order they have in the file. At least one KEY is needed.

## stats

`tabula stats FILE COLUMN...` prints one row per COLUMN, in the order asked, with the columns `column`, `count`, `min`,
`max`, `mean`, `median`. The statistics are over the cells of that column that are not empty (a cell of only
whitespace counts as empty); all of those must be numbers (mistake as in `sort` otherwise). `count` is how many there
are. `min` and `max` print as in `group`; `mean` and `median` are rounded half up to two decimals and always printed
with two (the median of an even count is the mean of the two middle numbers, taken exactly). With no numbers at all the
row is `COLUMN`, `0` and four empty cells. At least one COLUMN is needed.

"""tabula.engine -- the table model, the transforms, the output formats and the command line.

This is the one module every command lives in. A command is a function `cmd_NAME(args, opts)` that gets the
positional arguments (a list of strings) and the options (a dict) and returns a Table, which `main` then prints in the
format asked for (`--format text|csv|json`, text by default). A mistake in a file or in a request raises TabulaError
(exit status 1); a command line that is not shaped right raises UsageError (exit status 2).
"""
import csv
from contextlib import contextmanager
import io
import json
import os
import re
import sys
import unicodedata
from decimal import (Decimal, InvalidOperation, ROUND_HALF_UP, ROUND_FLOOR, ROUND_CEILING, ROUND_DOWN, getcontext,
                     localcontext)

from .errors import TabulaError, UsageError

PROG = "tabula"
FORMATS = ("text", "csv", "json")
OPTIONS = {"format": FORMATS, "kind": ("inner", "left"), "keep": ("first", "last")}
DEFAULTS = {"format": "text", "kind": "inner", "keep": "first"}
getcontext().prec = 60

NUMBER = re.compile(r"[+-]?(?:\d+(?:\.\d*)?|\.\d+)")


# --- numbers -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def to_decimal(text):
    """The Decimal a cell holds, or None when it is not a plain decimal number (no exponent, no thousands marks)."""
    text = text.strip()
    if not NUMBER.fullmatch(text):
        return None
    try:
        return Decimal(text)
    except InvalidOperation:
        return None


def fmt_decimal(number):
    """A Decimal as plain text: no exponent, no negative zero."""
    text = format(number, "f")
    if text.startswith("-") and not text.strip("-0."):
        text = text[1:]
    return text


@contextmanager
def _wide(numbers, extra=10):
    """A local context wide enough to add up (or divide) these Decimals without losing a digit."""
    digits = sum(len(n.as_tuple().digits) + abs(n.as_tuple().exponent) for n in numbers)
    with localcontext() as ctx:
        ctx.prec = max(getcontext().prec, digits + extra)
        yield ctx


def fmt_2dp(number):
    """A Decimal rounded half up to two decimals, always printed with two."""
    with _wide([number]):
        return fmt_decimal(number.quantize(Decimal("0.01"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))


def _need_number(value):
    number = to_decimal(value)
    if number is None:
        raise TabulaError("%r is not a number" % value)
    return number

    if arg is None or not arg.isdigit():

    return int(arg)


def _need_decimal_arg(arg, name):
    number = None if arg is None else to_decimal(arg)
    if number is None:
        raise TabulaError("%s needs a number argument, got %r" % (name, arg))
    return number


def _no_arg(name, arg):
    if arg is not None:
        raise TabulaError("%s takes no argument, got %r" % (name, arg))


def _need_text(arg, name):
    if arg is None:
        raise TabulaError("%s needs an argument" % name)
    return arg


# --- the table -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

class Table:
    """Column names and rows of strings. `source` names where it came from, for messages."""

    def __init__(self, columns, rows, source="<table>"):
        self.columns = list(columns)
        self.rows = [list(r) for r in rows]
        self.source = source

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.rows)

    def index(self, name):
        """Position of a column; TabulaError when there is none."""
        try:
            return self.columns.index(name)
        except ValueError:
            raise TabulaError("%s: no column %r (columns: %s)" % (self.source, name, ", ".join(self.columns)))

    def column(self, name):
        at = self.index(name)
        return [row[at] for row in self.rows]

    def dicts(self):
        return [dict(zip(self.columns, row)) for row in self.rows]

    def with_rows(self, rows, columns=None):
        return Table(self.columns if columns is None else columns, rows, self.source)


def parse_text(text, source):
    """CSV text into a Table. Blank lines are ignored; every row must have as many fields as the header."""
    if text.startswith("﻿"):
        text = text[1:]
    reader = csv.reader(io.StringIO(text, newline=""))
    columns, rows = None, []
    try:
        for fields in reader:
            if not fields:
                continue
            if columns is None:
                for name in fields:
                    if not name.strip():
                        raise TabulaError("%s: line %d: empty column name" % (source, reader.line_num))
                if len(set(fields)) != len(fields):
                    raise TabulaError("%s: line %d: duplicate column name" % (source, reader.line_num))
                columns = fields
                continue
            if len(fields) != len(columns):
                raise TabulaError("%s: line %d: expected %d fields, found %d"
                                  % (source, reader.line_num, len(columns), len(fields)))
            rows.append(fields)
    except csv.Error as exc:
        raise TabulaError("%s: line %d: %s" % (source, reader.line_num, exc))
    if columns is None:
        raise TabulaError("%s: no header line" % source)
    return Table(columns, rows, source)


def load(path):
    """Read a CSV file (UTF-8, optional byte order mark, LF or CRLF) into a Table."""
    try:
        with open(path, "rb") as fh:
            raw = fh.read()
    except OSError as exc:
        raise TabulaError("%s: cannot read: %s" % (path, exc.strerror or exc))
    try:
        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        raise TabulaError("%s: not valid UTF-8" % path)
    return parse_text(text, path)

def render_text(table):
    cells = [table.columns] + table.rows
    widths = [max(len(row[i]) for row in cells) for i in range(len(table.columns))]
    lines = ["  ".join(cell.ljust(width) for cell, width in zip(row, widths)).rstrip() for row in cells]
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def render_csv(table):
    out = io.StringIO()
    writer = csv.writer(out, lineterminator="\n")
    writer.writerow(table.columns)
    writer.writerows(table.rows)
    return out.getvalue()


def render_json(table):
    return json.dumps(table.dicts(), ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"


RENDERERS = {"text": render_text, "csv": render_csv, "json": render_json}

+

python3 - <<'P'
big="9"*5000; small="0."+"0"*4999+"1"

import subprocess, os, json
from decimal import Decimal, getcontext
getcontext().prec=20000
big=Decimal("9"*5000); small=Decimal("0."+"0"*4999+"1")
def run(*a):
    r=subprocess.run(["python3","-m","tabula",*a,"--format","json"],capture_output=True,text=True)
    return r.returncode, (json.loads(r.stdout) if r.returncode==0 else r.stderr[:300])
rc,o=run("group","huge.csv","k","sum:v","min:v","max:v","mean:v")
print("group rc",rc)
print(" sum a ok", Decimal(o[0]["sum_v"])==big+small, "E" in o[0]["sum_v"])
print(" sum b ok", Decimal(o[1]["sum_v"])==-big+1)
print(" min/max a", o[0]["min_v"]==format(small,"f"), o[0]["max_v"]=="9"*5000)
print(" mean a", o[0]["mean_v"][-10:], len(o[0]["mean_v"]), "expected", ((big+small)/2).quantize(Decimal("0.01"),rounding="ROUND_HALF_UP").to_eng_string()[-10:])

from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP
vals=sorted([big,small,-big,Decimal(1)])
mean=sum(vals)/4; med=(vals[1]+vals[2])/2
print(" mean ok", Decimal(o[0]["mean"])==mean.quantize(Decimal("0.01"),rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP), "median ok", Decimal(o[0]["median"])==med.quantize(Decimal("0.01"),rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))
rc,o=run("pivot","huge.csv","k","k","v"); print("pivot same rc",rc,o if rc else "")
open("huge2.csv","w").write("r,c,v\nx,a,%s\nx,a,%s\n"%(big,small))
rc,o=run("pivot","huge2.csv","r","c","v"); print("pivot rc",rc, Decimal(o[0]["a"])==big+small)
rc,o=run("sort","huge.csv","v:num"); print("sort rc",rc,[r["v"][:3] for r in o])
rc,o=run("filter","huge.csv","v>"+"9"*4999); print("filter rc",rc,[r["v"][:3] for r in o])
rc,o=run("filter","huge.csv","v=="+"9"*5000+".0"); print("filter eq",rc,len(o))
P

content.text:
I signed off PRD #1 (label `reviewed` added) and filed the two output bugs I found as #4.

- **Tests:** all 157 tests pass on Python 3.13 and 3.9 at `ef14fa0`, and I recorded that commit on PRD #1. `pip install .` in a fresh venv gives a working `tabula` command and `import tabula`.
- **Brief check:** I ran each concrete rule in the original request as a command on a small file, and every one behaved as specified. The robustness checks also passed: byte order mark, invalid UTF-8, CRLF and lone CR line endings, form feed and U+2028 inside fields, empty option values, 5000-digit numbers through all the arithmetic, output piped into `head -1`, and output to `/dev/full`.
- **Issue #4, two bugs for one lane to fix:**
  1. A column whose name starts with `-` can't be named as a KEY, COLUMN or CONDITION: `-x` is rejected as an unknown option (exit 2), and `--` isn't accepted either. The brief keeps "unknown option exits 2" for existing behaviour, so the suggested fix is to accept `--` to end options, not to change how `-x` is read.
  2. In `group`, two aggregates can end up with the same column name once `:` becomes `_` (`sum:a:b` and `sum:a_b` both become `sum_a_b`). The table then has duplicate columns, and JSON output silently drops one of them. It should exit 1, as `group` already does when an aggregate's name matches BY.
- **Skipped steps:** the security audit is off for this fleet and the PRD has no Quality bar, so neither ran.

I left PRD #1 open; the engine closes it once #4 is done. This pass opened no PRs.
